# Independent audit: flat radius strictification and shared-cap escape

**PASS.** I independently read every section of
candidate 2c18dd3b9615c3c4, its
canonical physical-Hessian dependency, and its exact verifier.
No mathematical repair is needed.

## Flatness and the correct uniform margin

For centered homothetic fibers, every anchored Minkowski inclusion
is exactly the corresponding scalar radius inequality. The identity
\[
 \phi(z)-\sum_p\alpha_p\phi(p)
   =\sum_p\alpha_p|p-z|^2,\qquad \phi(p)=R-|p|^2,
\]
has the stated sign. Multiplication by the positive common factor
\(\lambda(\epsilon)\) preserves every such inequality.
The normalization fixes \(\sum s_z^d\) exactly. Because each fixed
canonical cylindrical cap cuts the same fraction \(\Gamma_d\) from
every positive multiple of the centered simplex, it fixes every
selected cap mass exactly as well. No cap plane moves in this stage.

The uniform margin is asserted on representations **excluding the
target**. Their variance is at least the squared minimum distance
between distinct bases. If a representation has target self-weight
\(\alpha_z<1\), its remaining weights, divided by \(1-\alpha_z\),
again represent the target. Thus the normalized representation has
the uniform gap even as the original self-weight tends to one.
The identity representation is exempt. The note never incorrectly
assigns a uniform positive gap to those unnormalized near-identity
representations.

## All nearby fibers are actually compatible

The support-function inequalities in (7) are valid because
\(\rho B\subset K\), so \(h_K(u)\ge\rho\) for unit \(u\).
The scale \(s_z-\eta/\rho\) is positive by the definitions of
\(\Delta\) and \(\eta\).
For every excluded-target representation, the entire perturbed
Minkowski combination lies in
\[
 (s_z-\Delta+\eta/\rho)K
 \Subset (s_z-\eta/\rho)K
 \subset L_z.
\]
Both scales are positive and their difference is
\(\Delta-2\eta/\rho>0\). This proves a uniform strict inclusion for
all unit normals and all representations, not merely a finite list.
The same argument also covers a vertex target vacuously.

For a general representation in the hull, normalize the terms other
than the target, apply that inclusion, then combine with its possible
own-fiber term using convexity of \(L_z\). This proves exact fiber
equality, including representations with self-weight. Lattice
completeness of \(P\) prevents additional integer bases. The inball
inside every \(L_z\), together with full affine base rank, proves
full dimension of the realizing hull. Thus the later physical
motions occur inside a genuine common open feasibility neighborhood.

## Weighted physical escape

I checked the exact proper-simplex cap formula and the positive
physical lift in the cited canonical-simplex-physical-hessian-inertia.md.
For the zero-sum vector \(c\), the displayed off-diagonal matrix has
column sums \(c\); adding diagonal \(-c\) makes it physical. Its full
row sums are \(-dm\,c/(dm-1)\), and its positive normalized Hessian
is \(q_d\|c\|^2\), with the stated \(q_d>0\) for \(d\ge2\).

Scaling the second chosen fiber's velocity by \(-V_p/V_q\) cancels
every global first cap derivative exactly, despite unequal fiber
volumes. Its squared scaling yields
\[
 H=q_d\|c\|^2(V_p+V_p^2/V_q)>0.
\]
The right inverse (13) has zero column sums, trace \(T\), and row
sums \(R\), because \(\sum R_i=0\). Its derivative is the requested
vector in actual volume units; the factor \(V_p\) is retained.
Applying it to \(-e-q_i\) therefore gives
\[
 C_i''=-e,\qquad M''=H-e/\Gamma_d=H/2
\]
when \(e=\Gamma_d H/2\). The polynomial vertex path and uniform
proper-cap analyticity make these strict actual improvements.
The preceding open feasibility neighborhood pays compatibility
throughout this path.

## Boundary cases and scope

The two-stage argument fixes a positive strictification parameter
first, then chooses the improving path short enough to stay inside
its open neighborhood. It makes no unsupported uniform path-length
claim as the strictification parameter tends to zero.
Finite convex hulls depend continuously on their compact fibers,
so the stated neighborhood conclusion for those hulls is valid.

The affine-centroid shear preserves every integer base and has
continuous fiber Jacobian one. For deficient affine base rank,
the lattice in the integer-spanned direction space is saturated;
the stated translation and unimodular normalization are valid.
The result is explicitly relative-dimensional and does not claim
an unrelated full-ambient completion.

The dimension-one exception is necessary: its two opposite
canonical caps partition the mixed measure up to null boundaries,
so retaining both original budgets bounds total mass by its original
value. The flat strictification itself still works in dimension one.
The escape assumes at least two positive fibers and \(d\ge2\).

Only the selected shared canonical group is preserved. Its budget
need not be critical depth, other cap budgets may change, and this
does not classify OC extremizers. The affine-centroid source class
was already OC-safe; the result concerns actual compatibility and
shared-cap stability.

## Exact verification

Reran successfully with the standard Python interpreter:

    python3 supporting computation verify_flat_radius_strictification_and_shared_escape.py

It checks 64 excluded-target Jensen relations, exact normalized
mass/cap identities for dimensions 1 through 8, and six actual
compatible unequal-volume physical escapes for dimensions 2 through 7.
The common potentially algebraic normalization is tracked by its
exact rational \(d\)-th power. Actual midpoint inclusion is verified
on every relevant vertex pair. The all-dimensional conclusions rest
on the displayed proofs, not on those finite checks.
